properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued July 29 at 4:32PM MDT until July 29 at 7:30PM MDT by NWS Denver CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Central Adams County in northeastern Colorado...

* WHEN...Until 730 PM MDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...

- At 432 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly in the advisory area. Between 1 and 1.5 inches of rain
have fallen.

- This includes the following streams and drainages...
Wolf Creek, Antelope Creek, Comanche Creek, Lost Creek, Sand
Creek, West Sand Creek, Kiowa Creek and Mule Creek. Additional
rainfall amounts up to 0.5 inches are expected over the area.
This additional rain will result in minor flooding.

- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Mainly rural areas of Central Adams County.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued July 29 at 4:31PM MDT until July 29 at 5:30PM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
At 431 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms which produced
heavy rain across the warned area have ended. Between 1 and 3 inches
of rain have fallen. Flooding impacts will continue, but no
additional rainfall is expected at this time. Flash flooding will
continue until the water has a chance to recede.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, rural roads and
normally dry washes, as well as other poor drainage and
low-lying areas.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Victor.

This includes the following streams and drainages...
West Beaver Creek, Middle Beaver Creek, Wilson Creek and Bison
Creek their tributaries.

properties.headline: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued July 29 at 4:27PM MDT until July 29 at 5:00PM MDT by NWS Denver CO
properties.description:
At 427 PM MDT, severe thunderstorms were located along a line from 5
miles west of Wiggins to near Adena, or along a line from 20 miles
west of Fort Morgan to 17 miles southwest of Fort Morgan, moving
northeast at 20 mph.

HAZARD...60 mph wind gusts and small hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Expect damage to roofs, siding, and trees.

Locations impacted include...
Wiggins and Hoyt Beet Dump.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued July 29 at 4:18PM MDT until July 29 at 5:30PM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
FFWPUB

The National Weather Service in Pueblo has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
North Central Fremont County in central Colorado...

* Until 530 PM MDT.

* At 418 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated new thunderstorms producing
heavy rain moving into the warned area. Between 1 and 3 inches of
rain have fallen from earlier thunderstorms. The expected rainfall

to 2 inches are possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, roads, and
normally dry washes, as well as other poor drainage and
low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Mainly rural areas of North Central Fremont County.

This includes the following streams and drainages...
Miller Creek, and South Tallahassee Creek

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued July 29 at 4:15PM MDT until July 29 at 7:00PM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
FFWGJT

The National Weather Service in Grand Junction has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
East Central Ouray County in southwestern Colorado...

* Until 700 PM MDT.

* At 415 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the Gold Mountain burn scar. Between 0.3 and 0.8
inches of rain have fallen. The expected rainfall rate is 1 to 2
inches in 1 hour. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly.

Excessive rainfall over the burn scar will result in debris flow
moving through the Cow Creek. The debris flow can consist of rock,
mud, vegetation and other loose materials.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms
producing flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
country roads, streets and underpasses.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
mainly rural areas of East Central Ouray County
